profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This is a roughly 200 million dollar private enterprise data center in Sarpy County, Nebraska, in the La Vista and Papillion area south of Omaha, built by Travelers Insurance, part of The Travelers Companies, a Hartford, Connecticut headquartered property casualty insurer. The project was developed under the code name Project Oasis before Travelers was publicly identified as the company behind it, a common practice for large corporate data center projects negotiating incentives and land deals before revealing their identity. Local and trade press, including Data Center Dynamics, Insurance Journal, and the Omaha World-Herald, covered the facility opening around 2015 as part of a broader wave of large data center construction in Sarpy County during the 2010s. As an enterprise private data center for Travelers own internal insurance operations, including policy administration, claims processing, and disaster recovery, the facility is not marketed for third party colocation, and no specific critical IT megawattage figure beyond the roughly 200 million dollar construction cost was found published. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading: Travelers Insurance, part of The Travelers Companies, a Hartford, Connecticut headquartered property casualty insurer, opened a roughly 200 million dollar private enterprise data center in Sarpy County, Nebraska, in the La Vista and Papillion area south of Omaha. The project was developed under the code name Project Oasis before Travelers was publicly identified as the company behind it, a common practice for large corporate data center projects seeking to negotiate incentives and land deals before revealing their identity. Local and trade press, including Data Center Dynamics, Insurance Journal, and the Omaha World-Herald, covered the facility's opening around 2015, describing it as part of a broader wave of large data center construction in Sarpy County during the 2010s that also drew other major corporate and hyperscale projects to the area, reflecting the county's relatively low disaster risk, available land, and utility incentives. As an enterprise private data center built by Travelers for its own internal insurance operations, including policy administration, claims processing, and disaster recovery, the facility is not marketed for third party colocation or public capacity, and no specific critical IT megawattage figure beyond the roughly 200 million dollar construction cost was found published for it during this research.
